Priya / Karthik — initial analysis attached. TL;DR:
- Recommended pilot: 3 months, 2x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to embeddings (estimated steady-state cost offset vs hosted: ~22% improvement per embedding token with caching and quantization).
- Commit bands: three tiers for 6/12/18 month terms; the 12-month band yields the best blended per-token price and includes a 10% uplift credit for the pilot period.
- Risk controls: automatic fallback to hosted chat model if latency exceeds 150ms P95 for 3 consecutive 5-min windows; we'll keep prefix cache warm for top 20 embeddings to reduce cold-start tail.

Sam — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Fallback & session continuity:
- Fallback is at the request-routing layer, not the session layer: requests will be routed to a hosted chat variant only when the routing policy detects sustained P95 > 150ms for the dedicated chat nodes.
- We'll preserve session continuity by forwarding a minimal session context and the last 3 user turns in the routed request; that keeps recommender context intact. We also include a 60-second sticky window so short blips won't trigger a route.

2) Cache warm time:
- Based on your Q3 distribution, cold-set for the top 20 prefixes is < 90s (with pre-warm hooks). For the broader corpus, steady-state P95 improves over 12–36 hours as we observe the production hit pattern and keep hot rows resident.

3) Right-to-scale clause:
- Proposed language: Quokka may request scaling increments at pre-agreed breakpoints (50%, 100% of pilot capacity) with a 30-day notice; pricing for those breakpoints is fixed in the commitment schedule. I'll attach the clause as part of the amendment.

Next steps:
- I attached the updated proposal (proposal-embeddings-pilot.pdf) with the fallback language and scaling clause.
- If that aligns, we can: 1) launch the 3-month pilot starting Dec 1, 2) finalise the 12-month commitment amendment, and 3) include a one-time 10% pilot credit on embedding billables.
